rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections – Just Cause for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A San Diego landlord may end a tenancy only for an at-fault cause (e.g., nonpayment, lease breach, nuisance) or a good-faith no-fault cause (owner move-in, withdrawal from market, government order, demolition/substantial remodel). For no-fault terminations the landlord must give written notice and pay relocation assistance of two months' rent (three months if the tenant is a senior or disabled), or waive that rent.
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador de San Diego solo puede terminar un arrendamiento por una causa atribuible al inquilino (p. ej., falta de pago, incumplimiento del contrato, molestias) o por una causa de buena fe sin culpa del inquilino (mudanza del propietario, retiro del mercado, orden gubernamental, demolición o remodelación sustancial). En las terminaciones sin culpa debe dar aviso por escrito y pagar asistencia de reubicación equivalente a dos meses de renta (tres meses si el inquilino es mayor de edad o tiene discapacidad), o condonar esa renta.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental tenancies over 30 days in the City of San Diego, including Section 8 units. Exempt: housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8); owner-occupied single-family homes (up to two bedrooms/ADUs rented) and owner-occupied duplexes; shared-facility rentals with the resident landlord; mobilehomes under the Mobilehome Residency Law; dormitories, hospitals, care facilities, transitional housing; and separately alienable units not owned by a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, with written exemption notice in the lease.
rules.exemptions: Certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; affordable/subsidized housing; owner-occupied single-family and duplex; shared-facility rentals; mobilehomes under MRL; institutional housing; alienable-title units with non-corporate landlord and written notice.
rules.key_value: Relocation assistance: 2 months' rent (3 months if senior/disabled); notice 30 or 60 days; right to re-rent offer for 5 years
rules.penalty: Landlord is liable for at least three times actual economic damages for wrongful eviction, at least three times required relocation assistance plus damages, possible attorney's fees, and non-compliant termination notices are void.
rules.caveat: Section 98.0704 and related sections were amended effective 2024-03-28 (O-21769); original ordinance effective 2023-06-24.
